subject: maths
title: Multiplication: fast repeated adding
intro: Multiplication is a shortcut for adding the same number many times. Instead of adding 4 + 4 + 4 slowly, you can say '3 times 4' and get the answer faster. Once you see multiplication as repeated adding — and as rows and columns — the times tables stop being something to fear and start to make sense.

sections.heading: Times means groups of
body: The times sign **×** means 'groups of'. So **3 × 4** means 'three groups of four', which is 4 + 4 + 4 = 12. Multiplication is just **repeated addition** written the short way, and it saves a lot of time when the groups are big.
A clear way to picture it is an **array** — rows and columns of dots. Three rows of four dots is 3 × 4, and you can count 12 dots altogether.

sections.heading: Order doesn't matter
body: Just like adding, multiplication can be done in **any order** and gives the same answer. **3 × 4** and **4 × 3** both equal 12 — three rows of four has the same number of dots as four rows of three, just turned on its side.
This is really useful: it halves how many facts you need to learn, because knowing 6 × 7 also gives you 7 × 6. It also lets you multiply in whichever order is easier for you.

steps: 5 × 3 means five groups of three (or three groups of five).

sections.heading: Learning the tables, and handy tricks
body: The **times tables** are just the answers to these facts, and knowing them by heart makes all later maths faster. A few tricks help: multiplying by **10** just adds a zero (7 × 10 = 70); multiplying by **2** is doubling; multiplying by **5** gives answers that always end in 0 or 5; and anything times **1** stays the same, while anything times **0** is 0.
Practise a little each day and the facts stick. They are the toolkit you'll reach for in division, fractions, area, and almost everything ahead.

practice.explain: The × sign means 'groups of', so 3 × 4 is three groups of four, which is 4 + 4 + 4 = 12.
Multiplication is repeated adding: three groups of four is 4 + 4 + 4 = 12.
Order doesn't matter in multiplication, so 7 × 6 is also 42.
Multiplying by 10 just adds a zero: 7 × 10 = 70.

summary: Multiplication (×) means 'groups of' — it is fast repeated adding, e.g. 3 × 4 = 4 + 4 + 4 = 12.
Picture it as an array of rows and columns of dots.
Order doesn't matter: 3 × 4 = 4 × 3, which halves the facts to learn.
Tricks: ×10 adds a zero, ×2 doubles, ×5 ends in 0 or 5, ×1 stays the same, ×0 is 0.
